newsitem.title: USA: 3M sees strong Q4, continued dollar impact.
newsitem.headline: 3M sees strong Q4, continued dollar impact.

text.p: Minnesota Mining & Manufacturing Co said the stronger U.S. dollar will continue to have an impact on earnings, but the company expects solid sales and earnings growth in the fourth quarter.

"We will benefit from new products, our customer satisfaction efforts, increased penetration of international markets and ongoing productivity improvement," said L.D. DeSimone, chairman and chief executive officer.
The diversified manufacturer on Friday reported income from continuing operations for the quarter ended September 30 of $398 million, up 17.4 percent from the year-ago quarter.

Earnings per share from continuing operations were $0.95, up from $0.81 last year. Both 1996 third-quarter figures were records for any quarter, 3M said. "Changes in currency exchange rates reduced earnings for the quarter by about $0.05 a share, or about six percent," the company said.
Third-quarter sales were $3.62 billion, up 7.5 percent from the same quarter last year. Excluding changes in currency exchange rates, sales rose about 11 percent, 3M said.
"Strong momentum in 3M's financial performance continued in the third quarter. Double-digit volume growth and healthy productivity gains drove our record results," DeSimone said.

3M said unit sales increased about 10 percent -- 12 percent outside the United States and more than seven percent in the United States. 3M companies Asia, Latin America and Canada posted double-digit volume increases.

"Unit sales in Europe increased more than seven percent, despite continued economic softness in major European countries," 3M said. "In the United States, growth was led by 3M's industrial and consumer sector."
"Looking ahead, we expect solid sales and earnings growth again in the fourth quarter," DeSimone said.
